key_insight: This paper shows that an attention graph neural network can be trained without labeled simulation data by directly minimizing finite-volume residuals on the mesh. In simple terms, the model learns the physics of 3D thermo-fluid fields from the governing equations instead of expensive solver-generated examples.
problem_solved: Traditional training for thermo-fluid surrogate models depends on large volumes of labeled data from numerical solvers, which are costly to compute and store. The paper addresses the challenge of building accurate 3D field predictors without paying that data-generation cost.
method: Represent the thermo-fluid domain as a mesh-based graph and use an attention GNN to model local and long-range interactions.
Compute finite-volume method residuals of the governing equations directly on the mesh as the training signal.
Optimize the network in a label-free way, removing the need for paired input-output simulation data.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in scientific computing, this enables physics-informed surrogate modeling when labeled data is scarce or expensive. It can significantly reduce preprocessing, storage, and simulation costs while preserving consistency with the underlying PDEs.
visual_elements: A mesh-to-graph diagram showing nodes, edges, and attention weights.
A pipeline graphic: governing equations -> FVM residuals -> GNN training -> predicted thermo-fluid field.
Side-by-side comparison of labeled training vs. label-free residual training.
Heatmap or contour plots of 3D temperature/flow fields with predicted vs. reference outputs.
paper_title: Label-Free Finite-Volume-Residual Training of Attention Graph Neural Networks for Coupled Thermo-Fluid Fields
paper_authors: Tianyu Li, Zhiwei Cao, Qingang Zhang, Ruihang Wang, Binyang Song
